scientific_name: Mandevilla x amabilis 'Sun Parasol Giant Crimson'

planting.note: Set out container plants after all frost danger has passed and soil has warmed, giving this extra-vigorous selection a large trellis or arbor to fill.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with a sturdy trellis, arbor, or fence, since this is one of the larger-growing Sun Parasol selections. Giant Crimson produces oversized, deep red-crimson trumpet flowers in heavy flushes from late spring through fall on vigorous twining stems. Feed monthly with a balanced fertilizer during active growth and keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged. In frost-prone zones grow in a large container and bring indoors to a bright spot before temperatures drop below 40°F.

scientific_name: Mandevilla x amabilis 'Sun Parasol Pretty Pink'

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed and frost risk has passed, siting near a trellis or obelisk to support its twining growth.

directions: Grow in full sun to light afternoon shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, watering deeply whenever the top inch of soil dries. Pretty Pink bears clear soft-pink trumpet flowers continuously from spring through frost and holds its color well even in intense summer heat. Pinch young growth to encourage branching and heavier bloom, and feed regularly with a phosphorus-rich fertilizer to sustain flowering. Overwinter containers indoors in cold climates, since this cultivar has no frost tolerance.

planting.note: Set out after last frost in a warm, sheltered spot with a trellis or stake, since Rio series plants are more compact than Sun Parasol types.

directions: Plant in full sun in rich, well-drained soil, giving Rio Red a small trellis or allowing it to trail from a hanging basket, since the Rio series is more compact and self-branching than older mandevilla lines. Bright red trumpet flowers appear in flushes all summer with minimal deadheading required. Water when the soil surface dries and fertilize every two to three weeks during the growing season. Bring indoors well before the first fall frost, as this cultivar has no cold hardiness.

planting.note: Transplant after frost danger passes into a container or bed with support, as this compact Rio series selection suits patio culture.

directions: Site in full sun with rich, well-drained soil and moderate humidity; Rio Pink produces abundant clear-pink trumpet blooms on a naturally bushy, self-branching habit that needs little pinching to stay full. Water thoroughly when soil begins to dry and feed with a balanced liquid fertilizer every few weeks through the growing season. Its compact size makes it well suited to large containers or mixed patio plantings. Protect from any temperature below 40°F by moving containers indoors.

planting.note: Transplant after soil has warmed following the last frost, spacing plants to fill in as a compact flowering mound.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and water regularly during establishment, then reduce to moderate watering once roots are settled. Graffiti Pink forms a dense, compact mound covered in clustered star-shaped bright pink flowers that draw butterflies and hummingbirds all summer into fall. Deadhead spent flower clusters occasionally to encourage continuous rebloom and feed lightly every four to six weeks. Heat and humidity tolerant, it performs reliably through the hottest part of the Gulf Coast growing season.

planting.note: Set out transplants once frost danger has passed and nights stay reliably warm, spacing to form a solid flowering border.

directions: Grow in full sun in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, keeping soil evenly moist while plants establish. Graffiti Violet bears dense clusters of rich violet-purple star-shaped flowers on a naturally uniform, compact habit that needs no pinching to stay tidy. It tolerates heat and humidity exceptionally well and attracts butterflies and hummingbirds throughout the growing season. Fertilize lightly on a monthly schedule and remove faded flower clusters periodically to keep new buds forming.

planting.note: Transplant after last frost into warm soil, spacing plants close together for a solid mass of color.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, watering deeply and regularly until plants are established. Kaleidoscope Red is a dwarf, uniform selection bred for bedding and container use, producing vivid red star-shaped flower clusters continuously from late spring through the first fall frost. Its compact size and tight branching mean it holds its shape without pinching, making it ideal for mass plantings and borders. Feed monthly during the growing season and expect strong butterfly and hummingbird activity.

planting.note: Set out transplants after soil has warmed past last frost, spacing to allow the mounding habit to fill in.

directions: Site in full sun to very light afternoon shade in fertile, well-drained soil, watering consistently through establishment. Northern Lights produces clusters of soft white-to-pale-lavender star-shaped flowers that brighten mixed borders and pair well with brighter pentas colors nearby. The mounding habit stays neat with minimal maintenance and rebloom is continuous from late spring through fall. Fertilize lightly every few weeks and deadhead old clusters occasionally to keep fresh buds coming.

planting.note: Plant in a lean, well-drained site after frost danger passes, giving Torch Glow a sturdy fence or trellis to climb.

directions: Grow in lean, well-drained, slightly dry soil in full sun, since bougainvillea blooms most heavily when kept on the dry side and never overfed with nitrogen. Torch Glow produces intensely bright orange-red bracts in heavy waves whenever daylight hours shorten seasonally, with sporadic bloom between flushes in warm climates. Allow the soil to dry noticeably between waterings and prune immediately after each bloom flush to shape growth and encourage the next cycle. Protect from temperatures below 30°F, as stems can suffer dieback in hard freezes though the root system typically survives.
